:::{#thm-min-entropy-at-most-collision-entropy}
#### The min-entropy is at most the collision entropy

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv).
Then the [min-entropy](#def-min-entropy) is at most the [collision entropy](entropy.qmd#def-renyi-entropy):

$$\renyientropyf{\infty}{X} \le \renyientropyf{2}{X}.$$

:::

::: proof

Let $p_{\max} = \max_x \Pf{X = x}$.
Each [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $\Pf{X = x}$ is at most $p_{\max}$,
so $\Pf{X = x}^2 \le p_{\max} \, \Pf{X = x}$.
Sum over the values $x$:

$$\sum_x \Pf{X = x}^2 \le p_{\max} \sum_x \Pf{X = x}.$$

The probabilities sum to $1$,
so the [collision probability](entropy.qmd#def-collision-probability) is at most $p_{\max}$:

$$\P(X = X') = \sum_x \Pf{X = x}^2 \le p_{\max}.$$

The function $-\log$ is decreasing,
so taking it of both sides reverses the inequality:

$$-\log \P(X = X') \ge -\log p_{\max}.$$

The left side is $\renyientropyf{2}{X}$ and the right side is $\renyientropyf{\infty}{X}$.

:::
